Run a demographic simulation

Source: R/simulate.R
simulate.Rd

Advance a configured model and return a population that can initialize a later run. The C++ engine samples candidate waiting times across age bands (fertility cell clocks for births), executes at continuous times, and prioritizes death over birth on exact ties. Events execute chronologically. In on-demand mode all living females face the fertility schedule. Rate mode uses either overall rates for all women (with a warning), or separate union_type schedules. A union-formation process is required. With on-demand union formation, use the woman's current partner, or draw one from all eligible men using conditional-logit probabilities from the matching formula to form a union at the birth. Men must meet the configured minimum age (default 15 years). Known kin are excluded within the configured generation bound on each side of a common ancestor (default two). Hard group exclusions also apply. If no eligible man exists, cancel the birth by default. Explicitly set cancel_birth_if_no_match = FALSE to preserve it with unknown father. Rate initiation adds age- or duration-specific search events for unpartnered women only. Duration schedules for separated/widowed categories measure time since the most recent union ended; none remains age-specific. Failed attempts draw another waiting time. Widowhood cancels pending births and switches to unpartnered fertility; a new union switches to partnered fertility, preserving birth spacing. Unpartnered births do not trigger searches in rate mode. Instead, select a father using the same available male pool, screening and father_matching model (falling back to matching), without forming a union or reserving the man. A failed match cancels the birth unless explicitly allowed by the union process. Cancellation starts no new birth-spacing interval. On-demand mode rejects status schedules. Optional union_dissolution() adds one duration-dependent annual union hazard carried by the woman. It preserves the pending dissolution through births, ends the episode with end_reason = "dissolution", and restores unpartnered availability and fertility/search eligibility. Exact same-person ties select death, birth, dissolution, then search. Dissolution group_pair schedules and multipliers use symmetric pairings of both partners' groups. Rate-based formation optionally selects age/duration schedules using previous_union: none, separated, or widowed (or pooled none/dissolved). Duration origins and categories are recovered from recorded histories. Matching uses male-group weights recalibrated at each search; simulation warns once if any search needed approximate weights. A separate father model has its own preferences and delta target adjustments. Event initiation is unchanged. Optional cohabitation uses rate mode only: type is selected from cohab_prob before marriage/cohabitation-specific matching. Conversion retains partners and creates linked episodes, with same-person ties ordered death, birth, dissolution, conversion, search. Fertility input strata use union_type.

Usage

simulate(model, years, seed = NULL)

Arguments

model

A hammel_model containing a population, mortality, fertility, and union-formation processes, optionally union dissolution and group transitions. The population must have a finite end_time.

years

Nonnegative simulation duration in years; fractional years are supported, as are fractional population endpoints and calendar-rate bands.

seed

Optional integer seed. With a seed, the caller's RNG state is restored afterward. With NULL, the simulation advances the current RNG.

Value

A hammel_population with updated histories and endpoint, plus a simulation component recording run settings and birth/death counts, plus dissolutions when a dissolution process is configured.

Details

Optional group_transition() adds directed competing age- or duration-based moves, with optional sex and union-type strata. A move updates current group and affected event/pool/cell state, retaining ancestry. Grouped output always includes a transitions tibble; restarts preserve the full transition history.

Optional fertility hetfert = het_fert(cv, alpha) weights eligible mother selection within fixed-intensity cells. Supplied positive female weights are retained; absent weights are drawn under the simulation seed, and daughters inherit on the log scale. Output persons includes hetfert whenever enabled, and omits it whenever disabled, even if the input supplied weights.

Minimum birth spacing is configured in fertility() or set_fertility() and uses recorded maternal births, including on restart. Births are generated by cell-accounted fertility (D101; see fertility()): each one-year age/parity/union-type/group cell produces births at its input rate times all its members, assigned to an eligible member uniformly or proportionally to hetfert weights when enabled. Births that cannot occur because a cell has no eligible member are reported in simulation$unrealized_births. Fertility outside supplied bands is zero. Mortality must cover all ages for both sexes, ending at Inf.

Events are recorded at their sampled times in [start, start + years). Rates and all times remain in person-year and year units. Newborn group identity uses fertility's inheritance model (random parent by default, with maternal fallback), if groups are present; other newborn custom columns are missing. Grouped rate tables use each person's group (the woman's group for union searches). Ungrouped tables apply to everyone. Missing population groups in a grouped rate table are errors. Without population groups, each grouped table uses its first alphabetical group with a warning; this does not create group identities. Matching can use group predictors and pair effects. Existing custom columns and histories are preserved. Restarting samples new pending events and does not reproduce an uninterrupted run exactly. When ancestry is tracked, each newborn receives half of each parent's shares, with a missing parent contributing its half to unknown ancestry. Initial shares are retained, including on restart; grouped populations without shares initialize from recorded identities. No additional random draws are made.

Calendar-banded rates change within the same run at time_start/time_end boundaries, before same-time demographic events. Histories, birth spacing and duration origins persist. Pending candidates are resampled at boundaries; adding redundant rate boundaries need not preserve a fixed-seed trajectory. Calendar-banded cohab_prob is evaluated at the search instant; probability- only boundaries refresh role calibration while retaining pending event dates. Matching and inheritance arguments may be direct models or calendar schedules with time_start, time_end and list-column model. The current matching model is selected at partner/father choice and inheritance at birth. Model- only boundaries preserve pending events and earlier histories.

Examples

population <- create_baseline_population(100, max_age = 50)
model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_population(population) |>
  set_mortality(data.frame(sex = c("m", "f"), age_start = 0,
    age_end = Inf, rate = 0.01)) |>
  set_fertility(data.frame(age_start = 15, age_end = 50, rate = 0.1)) |>
  set_union_formation("on_demand",
    create_matching_model(~ age_difference, c(age_difference = 0)))
result <- simulate(model, years = 2, seed = 42)
result$simulation

#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $end_time
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $birth_interval
